summary: Requirements a pose research model must satisfy before capability D can be enabled. Every id is checked by backend/roomsense/inference/pose/gate.py. In this release no model is installed and no inference runtime is shipped, so capability D is DISABLED.

requirements.title: Valid manifest
requirements.description: configs/pose_model_manifest.json exists, is at most 256 KiB of UTF-8 JSON with no duplicate keys or non-finite numbers, uses schema roomsense-pose-manifest-v1 and passes strict validation (no unknown fields, no type coercion).

requirements.title: A model is installed
requirements.description: The manifest says installed: true and names model_id, source_url, source_commit, license, weights_path, weights_format, weights_sha256, input requirements, output keypoints, coordinate frame, training domain, validation evidence and compute needs.

requirements.title: Known licence
requirements.description: A licence is named for the weights and it is not 'unknown' (or none/unlicensed/NOASSERTION/TBD). Code licences do not automatically cover weights or datasets; the licence of the weights themselves must be stated.

requirements.title: Weights stored locally inside the app data directory
requirements.description: weights_path resolves (after following symlinks) inside the configured data directory. Nothing is downloaded at runtime.

requirements.title: Weights integrity
requirements.description: The weights file exists and its SHA-256 equals weights_sha256 in the manifest.

requirements.title: Safe weights format with a shipped runtime
requirements.description: Weights are safetensors or ONNX (never pickle-based formats such as .pt/.pth/.pkl/.joblib/.ckpt, which can execute code when loaded) and this build includes a reviewed inference runtime for that format. This release ships none.

requirements.title: Same CSI source as training
requirements.description: The runtime CSI source (chip family and LTF segment, e.g. esp32-classic-lltf) equals the one the model was trained on. CSI from different NICs is not interchangeable (different subcarrier grids, AGC, scaling and phase behaviour).

requirements.title: Same record format
requirements.description: The runtime record format (e.g. roomsense-rscsi-v1) equals the one the model's preprocessing expects.

requirements.title: Transmit antenna count
requirements.description: Transmit antennas per transmitter equal the trained configuration.

requirements.title: Receive antenna count
requirements.description: Receive antennas per receiver equal the trained configuration. Multi-antenna models cannot be fed single-antenna CSI by padding or copying channels.

requirements.title: Number of synchronised links
requirements.description: The number of simultaneously captured transmitter-to-receiver links equals the trained configuration.

requirements.title: Subcarrier count
requirements.description: The number of valid subcarriers per packet equals the trained configuration. Frames are never padded, truncated or interpolated to force a shape.

requirements.title: Packet rate
requirements.description: The measured (not configured) packet rate is within the manifest's tolerance of the trained rate.

requirements.title: Phase availability
requirements.description: If the model needs calibrated CSI phase, the runtime provides it. Separate ESP32 boards share no RF clock and this project does not process phase, so phase is unavailable here.

requirements.title: Independent test set
requirements.description: Reported metrics come from test data that shares no recording session, person or day with the training data. Random-frame or within-clip splits do not qualify.

requirements.title: Measured with this hardware in this environment
requirements.description: The metrics were measured with the user's own boards in the user's own room and wall configuration. Numbers copied from a paper do not transfer.

requirements.title: Real, named evaluation data
requirements.description: The evidence names the evaluation dataset, records metrics (e.g. PCK@0.2, MPJPE) and does not rely on synthetic data.

notes: Declared by this project (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, roomsense/csi_layouts.py), not measured by this file.
Classic chips (ESP32/-S2/-S3/-C3) with the lltf_only configuration deliver 64 LLTF positions, of which 52 are occupied subcarriers (k = -26..26 without DC).
The rate range is the configured transmit/ping rate; the gate compares against the measured rate.
Amplitude only: processing.use_phase is false and separate boards have no shared RF clock.

missing_for_this_hardware: No published Wi-Fi pose model found that was trained on single-antenna ESP32 LLTF amplitude CSI and released usable weights with independent evaluation.

The peer-reviewed Wi-Fi pose systems reviewed (DensePose From WiFi, Person-in-WiFi, Person-in-WiFi 3D, MM-Fi Wi-Fi modality) use Intel 5300 or Atheros NICs with 3 receive antennas per receiver, and DensePose From WiFi and Person-in-WiFi 3D use sanitised phase; this hardware has one antenna per board and no usable phase.

The community ESP32 pose projects reviewed either use 2 to 9 synchronised links (not one) or expect a 56-subcarrier input (not the 52 occupied LLTF subcarriers used here); all report only same-recording or random-split numbers, and they publish no weights, pickle-based checkpoints without a licence, or (RuView pose_v1) safetensors weights with a self-reported PCK@20 of about 3%.
No weights in a safe format (safetensors/ONNX) with a known licence exist for this hardware, and no inference runtime is shipped.
No independent, session/person/day-split evaluation measured with this project's boards in the user's room exists.
